To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the peptide microarray technology allows to describe a clinically relevant immune responses to B. pertussi infection and vaccination, and that the peptide microarrays may help to guide vaccine development by the description of the epitope signature responses.

(i) the serum antigen recognition profiles (‘the reactomes’) induced by B. pertussiss (Bp) infection and the DTP whole-cell (wc) vaccine are more similar to each other than to the reactomes of the acellular 5-component and 2-component (a2) Bp vaccines, and (ii) peptide microarray technology allows the detection of subtle differences between vaccine reactomes that may be relevant for vaccine development.
the peptide recognition pattern of serum antibodies induced by Bp infection or by Bp vaccines is unique for each group.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of unique Bp antigen recognition signatures of serum antibodies in children with whooping-cough or after vaccination with different Bp vaccines.
the identification of unique epitopes that are recognized by antibodies in the sera of children with whooping-cough or vaccinated with DPTwc, a5, or a2 vaccines.

the development of new vaccines, which will be based on the identification and characterization of the specific epitope antigens that are recognized by the host immune system during an infectious disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DPTa5, and DPTa2, and DT vaccines induce a different epitope recognition profile compared to whooping cough, and DTPwc.
the epitope recognition pattern induced by the whooping cough and whole-cell pertussis vaccines resembles each other more than to acellular pertussis vaccine.
the reactome of the whooping cough group was more similar to DTPwc, and the reactomes of the DTPa5 and DT groups were more similar to each other than to the other groups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified a unique recognition signature for each of the vaccination groups, and that DTPwc resembles the signature of children with whooping-cough more closely than the acellular vaccines, DPTa5 and a2.
the peptide microarray technology is a useful tool for vaccine development and that we have identified a unique peptide recognition pattern for each of the vaccination groups.
whooping cough and the DTPwc vaccine reactome are qualitatively similar, but the acellular vaccines differ significantly in their epitope recognition pattern.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the epitope recognition profile of the immune response to pertussis infection differs from that of vaccination.
the reactome induced by Bp vaccines is qualitatively different from that of the natural infection.
peptide microarray technology is a powerful tool to study the epitope recognition signature of the immune system in response to vaccination or disease.
